newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM unopposed as leader of his party.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM unopposed as leader of his party.

text.p: Czech Premier Vaclav Klaus, head of the senior partner in the ruling coalition, the centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS), remains unopposed as a candidate for the post of party chairman, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"Vaclav Klaus is the only candidate for the position," Jana Petrova, ODS's spokeswoman told Reuters four days ahead of the party's congress to elect the chairman and four vice-chairmen.
Petrova did not exclude a broader debate on ODS leadership during the party conference to be held on Friday and Saturday in Czech second city Brno.
"It depends on each speaker -- what will they say in their speeches -- but I think such a discussion will be held, but it is hard to guess," Petrova said.
Last summer, foreign minister and ODS vice-chairman Josef Zieleniec shocked many people when he publicly questioned Klaus's leadership.
In a widely-read newspaper interview, Zieleniec appealed for more voices to be heard in the party after the coalition lost its majority in June parliamentary elections.
The vigorously self-confident right-wing economist Klaus denied there was any rift in his party over his leadership style, suggesting the issue had been manufactured by the media.
He said Zieleniec's intervention "does not mean any confrontation of personalites within the party".
After the general elections, local analyst's forecast that Klaus's destiny would be determined by the results of mid-November Senate elections.
In those, ODS won 32 out of 81 Senate seats, and the ruling three-party coalition won a majority of 42 seats.
But because of extremely poor turnout -- only a third of eligible Czechs voted -- analysts say the Senate result meant little and Klaus's position seemed secure. -- Prague Newsroom 42-2-2423-0003
